question.note: Phrased as what the paper argues, but its subject is the spillover of the 'convicted criminal' advertisement onto perceptions of people with records (Q1); same call as the calibration note's question entry [0].

central_claim.note: Gives the ad's harm to perceptions and its improvement of feelings of representation; omits the counter-narrative's offset.

evidence.note: E2: total N and the three arms (no per-arm counts). E1 partial: survey experiment only; Democrats, pre-registration, Prolific and dates not stated in the claim.
The counter-narrative 'significantly ameliorated' the ad's negative effects (abstract wording, 'vastly ameliorated'): F2, a finding in the evidence slot.
Counter-narrative half of E3 (perspective of a formerly incarcerated representative); the ad stimulus is not described.

flags.text: 'The stigmatizing label led to a significant decrease' attributes the effect to the label; the stimulus was the mugshot with the label, and the paper says the two cannot be disentangled (p.17). The quote says 'the Trump advertisement'.
Says the counter-narrative increased perceptions by 0.83 SD without saying it preceded the ad and is compared with the ad alone (p.11, p.16). The quote keeps the qualification.
Says the ad increased perceived self-interest motives of officials; the paper finds the ad increased belief that officials are motivated by public service (p.11, beta = 0.130; p.15).

evidence.note: Only quote NOT IN PAPER. The counter-narrative half is also reversed (see [16]).

flags.text: Says the ad reduced perceived quality of Democratic representation; the ad increased it (p.11, p.15). The decrease the quote reports is the counter-narrative's, relative to the ad alone (F5).
Says the counter-narrative increased perceived complexity of representation. H1E was unsupported: no significant difference, and the estimate is negative (-0.062, p.11).

evidence.note: Only quote NOT IN PAPER; the value-of-representation half (H1C) is accurate but not gold.
Pre-registered hypotheses: the pre-registration part of E1.

flags.text: Says exposure to the ad increased support for the advertisement. No such comparison exists: ad support was asked only after exposure to the ad in every arm and is not in Table 3 (p.10-11).

evidence.note: The counter-narrative's decrease in ad support is F4 (misplaced).
Accurate: 'the most profound impact of the counter-narrative ... was on the perceptions' (p.11); not a gold answer.

flags.text: Says the counter-narrative 'reduced the negative perception of the quality of Democratic representation', i.e. improved it. The counter-narrative decreased perceived quality relative to the ad alone (p.11, beta = -0.332), as the quote says.

evidence.note: No credit. Wording is muddled; read as the reverse of F5.
